Upon the whole Matter, your Committee came to the following Resolutions.

1. Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Con*-mittcc, That the several Persons employed in the Business of Frame-work knitting, in the Town of Nottingham, who have petitioned against the Proceedings of the Conv-pany of Frame-work Knitters, have fully proved thfe Allegations of their Petition.

2. Resolved, Thac it is the Opinion of this Committee, Thac the Persons employed in the Trade and Bu-finess of Frame-work knitting, in the Towns and Parishei of Godalming, Guildford, Whitley, Thur/Iey, Hambleton, Compton, and other Places, in the County of Surry, who have petitioned against the Proceedings of the Company of Frame-work Knitters, have fully proved the Allegations of their Petition.

3. Rcfohed, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, Thac the By-laws of the Company of the Framework Knitters, incorporated by a Charter bearing Date the 19th Day of August, in the 15th Year of the Reign of King Charles the Second, are injurious and vexatious to the Manufacturers, and tend to the Discouragement of Industry, and to the Decay of the said Manufacture.

4. Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That many of the said By-laws are illegal, and contrary to the Liberty of the Subjedh

. Refiifoed^ That it is- the Opinion of this Committee, Thac the Powers granted by the said Charter are htirtful to the Trade, and tend to a Monopoly.

6. Resolved, That it is. the Opinion of this Committee, That the carrying on vexatious Ftofecvrtions against any Persons, Male 6r Female, for exercising the Arc and Mistery of Frame-work knitting, is hurtfid to the Manufacture, and destructive to the Trade of this Kingdom.

To all the Frame-work Knitters.

Since publishing the Address to the Frame-work Knitters, the 15th of duguft last, the Master, Wardens, and Assistants, of the Company, in London, have made an Order with respect to the Country, to the following Purport. <c That every Person in the Character of a Jour-u nevman, and who hires Frames of an Employer, may u be admitted, paying Five Shillings only, Two of which €t are to pay for the King's Stamps, which they ar£ obliged to use on every Admission, Two more for the <€ Clerk’s, and One for the Beadle's Fees." And Notice is hereby given, that on Yburjday, the 26th Instant, a Court , will be held at The Crown Innt on the Long Row,

Nottingham, for admitting all and every the Matters and Journeymen belonging to the Trade, who are desirous to take up their Freedom of the Company, these being the easiest Terms on which Admittances (which is the first Step to be taken, in order to form a Community) can possibly be granted; and, if duly encouraged amongst our-selves, will ^we think) effectually establith the Regulation so long wanted, and so much hoped for, notwithstanding the many Efforts of some of the Employers, who are ft riving against it, and at the same time pretend to be the Workmen's Friends; but how far such Conduct can be consistent with real Friendship to the Journeymen, we leave to their qy/n Judgments; and chat the Journeymen may not be further deceived by those who endeavour co lessen the Validity of the Company’s new By-laws (an attested Copy of which may be seen) it is thought proper to in-

form all the Journeymen, that the Orders, Rules, and Ordinances, of the Company of Frame work Knicters, made by the Master, Wardens and Assistants, of the said Company, on the 22d of May 1745, were since confirmed, pursuant to Act: of Parliament-, by the Right Honourable Philip Lord Hardwicke, the prefenc Lord High Chancellor of Great Britain, Sir William Lee Knight the present Lord Chief Justice of his Majesty’s Court of King's Bench, and Sir John Willes Knight, the present Lord Chief Justice of his Majesty’s Court of Common Pleas 5 and that no Journeymen may be discouraged at the Quarterage (although but Three Pence) we take-this Opportunity to acquaint them, that the Court will not expect it from any of the poor Men, many of whom a* this time (although not old) are scarce able to get Bread, it being thought sufficient to call on those who keep Frames or Apprentices. Then let us immediately agree to be of One Mind for this General Good, and heartily join, with One Voice, to proclaim the Court our Protection ! and no more Colts

& After the time above-mentioned, th^ Court will be held the First Yhurfday in every succeeding Month, beginning on Yhurjday the 2d of November next. t \

A Petition of Walter Stubbs of Bickbury, in the County of Salop, Gentleman, and John Dutton of Colehurst, in the said County, Gentleman* was presented to the House, and read; setting forth, That the Petitioners* being Lessees of divers Mines and Veins of Coal, in the Lordship of Hawarden, have, within these Twelve Months pad, at an Expence of One thousand Pounds, made and perfected a Frame or Timber Road from the said Works, to the new Channel of the River Dee, on Saltney Marsh, in the Parish and Lordship of Hawarden, which is of great and publick Benefit; and that, in case the Bill now depending in the House, for confirming Articles of Agreement between the Lord of the Manor of Hawarden and the River Dee Company, should not take effect, the Petitioners are informed, the said Work of Navigation will be deserted, and the Navigation thereof totally loft j whereby the Petitioners and many others, who have expended large Sums of Money (which intirely depend upon the Navigation of the said River) will be greatly injured and ruined: And therefore praying the House to give such due Encouragement to the said Company, as may enable them to preserve the Navigation of the said River.

Ordered, That the said Petition be referred to the Consideration of the Committee to whom the said Bill is committed.

A Petition of Jehu Philpet, on behalf of himself, and John Hutchinson and Thomas Hewit, was presented to the House, and read; letting forth. That the Petitioner hath been, for many Years, a considerable Dealer in the Tobacco Trade, and for about Six Years part hath continued the said Trade with the said John Hutchinson; and that the Petitioner and his said Partner, having suffered by great and unavoidable Lodes in their T radc, became considerably indebted upon several Bonds given to his Majesty for the Ctistoms and other Duties on Tobacco; and although the Petit oner and his said Partner have, from time to time, paid considerable Sums towards Discharge of the said Duties, they are ftiU Debtors to his Majesty on account of the said Duties, as appears by the Report of the proper Officers annexed to the Petition; and that such Lodes greatly reduced the Petitioner and his said Partner in their Circumstances, whereby they became considerably indebted to sundry other Persons, and, being unable to pay them their Debts, a CommifLon of Bankruptcy ififued out, and also a Process of Extent, against them, and the said Thomas Hewit and Edward Lee (who is since dead insolvent) their Sureties for Recovery of the said Debt to his Majesty; and that the Petitioner and his said Partner, and the said Thomas Hewit, are utterly unable to satisfy the said Debt, but are willing to make his Majesty the utmost Satisfaction in their Power, and hope, by the Assistance of their Friends, they may be enabled to compound the said Debt, if they may be permitted so to do: And praying the House to take the Premises into Consideration, and give Leave, That a Clause or Clauses maybe inserted in some Bill, to impower the Commissioners of his Majesty’s Treasury, or Lord High Treasurer, for the Time ocing, to compound with the Petitioner and his said Partner, and Surety, for the said Debt; or that they may be otherwise relieved, as to the House shall seem meet.

Mr. Chancellor of the Exchequer, by his Majesty’s Command, acquainted the House, That his Majesty, having been informed of the Contents of the said Petition, gives his Consent, That the Housetnay do therein as they shall think fir.

Ordered, That the said Petition be referred to the Consideration of a Committee of the whole House.

Resolved, That this House will. Tomorrow Morning, resolve itself into a Committee of the whole House, to consider of the said Petition.

A Message from his Majesty, by the Honourable Sir Henry Bellenden, Gentleman Usher of the Black Rod: Mr. Speaker,

The King commands this Honourable House to attend his Majesty, immediately, in the House of Peers.

Accordingly, Mr. Speaker, with the House, went up Royal Affect to attend his Majesty in the House of Peers; where his 10 Majesty was pleased to give the Royal Assent to the several publick and private Bills following; viz.

An Act for granting to his Majesty a certain Sum of Money, therein mentioned, out of the Sinking Fund; and for applying certain Surplus Monies remaining in the Exchequer, for the Service of the Year One thousand Seven hundred and Fifty-three; and for the further appropriating the Supplies granted in this Session of Parliament; and for enlarging the Time limited by an Act of the last Scfion of Parliament for subscribing Annuities after the Rate of Three Pounds per Centum per Annum, and Three Pounds Ten Shillings per Centum per Annum, into the joint Stock of Annuities; and for other Purposes therein mentioned.

An Act for continuing several Laws relating to the Puniftunent of Persons going armed, or disguised, in Defiance of the Laws of Customs or Excise, to the Drawback of the Duties upon Copper Bars exported, and to the Duties upon foreign-made Sail-Cloth 5 and also for Encouragement of the Silk Manufactures, and for taking off several Duties on Merchandizes exported, and forencoU-raging the Trade of the Sugar Colonies in America, and for vacating the Security for the Duty on Salt loft in any River, or in Port after shipped, and for enlarging the Time for proving the Loss of Salt, and for Relief of Masters of Ships, with respect to the Importation of Soap and Candles, contrary to an Act made in the Twenty-third Year of his Majesty’s Reign; and also for the more effectual Payment of the Bounties upon British-nrddc Sailcloth, and to impower the Commissioners of the Treasury to direct the Payment of the Bounty to John Henniker, and others, upon Four Ships fitted out for the Whale Fishery, and loft in the Greenland Seas, and also to Philip How, and others, upon Two Ships employed in the said Fishery, notwithstanding some of the Forms required by Law, in fitting out such Ships, were not complied with.

An Act for the better preventing of clandestine Marriages.

An Act to explain, amend, and continue, several Laws more effectually to prevent the Spreading of the Distemper which now rages amongst the horned Cattle in this Kingdom i for the more effectual paying the Expences of passing Vagrants; for obviating Doubts that mayarife touching the Keeping of Prisoners until the Prison of the Marshalsea of the Court of King’s Bench shall be rebuilt, or repaired; and for amending so much of the Act of the Twenty-fourth of his present Majesty for regulating the Commencement of the Year, and for correfing the Calendar now in Use, as relates to the time of Electing publick Officers of the City of Chester.

My Lords and Gentlemen,

THE Season of the Year is so far advanced, and the Business before you so entirely finished, that it is necessary to put an End to this Session of Parliament; the Zeal which you have shewn for my Person and Government, in all your Proceedings, calls for my sincere Thanks 3 and the Care and Assiduity you have exerted in making such Provisions as may advance the Commerce of my Subjects,

Mr. Speaker reported. That the House had attended his Majesty in the House of Peers, where his Majesty was pleased to make a most gracious Speech from the Throne to both Houses of Parliament; of which, Mr. Speaker said, he had, to prevent Mistakes, obtained a Copy: Which he read to the House; and is as followeth; viz.

My Lords and Gentlemen* -

I have called you together as early as your Attendance upon your private Affairs would admit 5 and 1 am confident that you are all met with the best Dispositions to give such Application and Dispatch to the Business of this Section as may be most conducive to the publick Utility. The Events of this Year have not made it necessary for me to offer any thing in particular to your Consideration relating to foreign Affairs. The Continuance of the publick Tranquillity and the general State of Europe remain upon the same Foot as when we last parted, and you may be assured of my Steadiness in pursuing the most effectual Measures to preserve to my People the Blessings of Peace. Gentlemen of the House of Commons,

I have nothing to ask of you, but the necessary Supplies for the ordinary Services of the ensuing Year, and such as have already been under your Consideration. I have ordered Estimates to be laid before you; and from the Experience I have had of your constant Regard for my Honour, and the Security as well as Ease of your Fellow Subjects, I entertain no Doubt of your making the proper Provisions for these Purposes.

My Lords and Gentlemen,

I am sorry to be obliged again to mention to you a Subject which reflects Dilho/iour upon the Nation, as well as creates great Danger and Mischicfto my good Subjects. It is with the utmost Regret 1 observe,that the horrid Crimes of Robbery and Murder are of late rather increased than diminished. I am sensible, that Works of Reformation are not to be cff'ected at once; but every body should contribute their best endeavours; and let me earnestly VoL. 26.

recommend it to you to continue your serious attention to this important Object. Wharibever shall be found expedient, either in this or any other Respect, for the Welfare and Happiness of my People, shall meet with my hearty Concurrence and Support.

Resolved, Nemine contradictnte, That an humble Address be presented to his Majesty, to return his Majesty the Thanks of this House for his most gracious Speech from the Throne; and to promise his Majesty, that we will not fail on our Parts to give such Application and Dispatch to the Business of this Section as may be most conducive to the publick Utility; to express our Satisfaction at the happy Continuance of the general Tranquillity, our Gratitude to his Majesty for his constant Attention to an Object so essential to the Interests of his People, and our Confidence in his Majesty’s Steadiness to pursue the most effectual Measures for preservingto us the many Blcfiings that rciult from it; to promise his Majesty, that We will chearfully raise such Supplies as shall be found necessary for the Services of the ensuing Year, and to testify to his Majesty how pleasing it is to us to receive freffi Marks of his gracious Approbation of our part Zeal and Regard for his Honour, as well as for the Security and Ease of our Fellow-Subjects; to declare our great Concern, that the Methods hitherto attempted to repress and prevent the horrid Crimes of Robbery and Murder, lo grievous as well as dishonourable to the Nation, have proved ineffectual; and to assure his Majesty, that however difficult the Talk may be to reform or even restrain the Desperate and Abandoned, we will nevertheless persevere in our serious Endeavours to find out, if possible,.a more adequate Remedy against such Enormities, being fully persuaded, from an uninterrupted Experience of his Majesty’s goodness, that we shall have not only his Majesty’s Concurrence, but also Support, in every Measure rhat shall be found expedient in this, or any other Respect, for the Welfare and Happiness of his People.

Ordered, That a Committee be appointed to draw up an Address to be presented to his Majesty upon the said Resolution:

Most gracious Sovereign,

We your Majesty’s most dutiful and loyal Subjects, the Commons of Great Britain in Parliament assembled, beg Leave to return your Majesty our humble Thanks for your most gracious Speech from the Throne.

And we assure your Majesty, that we will not fail on our Parts to give such Application ind Dispatch to the Business of this Session as may be m6ft conducive to the publick Utility.

The happy Continuance of the general Tranquillity calls upon us to express our Gratitude to your Majesty for your constant Attention to an Object so dfential to the Interest of your People, and we have the utmost Confidence in your Majesty’s Wisdom and Steadincfs, that you will pursue the most eftcdual Measures for preserving to this Naion the inestimable Bl. flings of Peace.

We beg Leave to allure your Majesty, that we will chearfully rajfc inch Supplies as shall be found necessary for the Services of the ensuing Year.

Nothing can be more pleasing to your faithful Commons, than to receive fresh Marks of your Majesty’s " gracious Approbation of our past Zeal and Regard for

your Honour, as well as for the Security and Ease of our Fellow-subjects.

We lament, with the deepest Concern, that the Methods hitherto attempted to repress and prevent the horrid > Crimes of Robbery and Murder, so grievous as well as dishonourable to this Nation, have proved ineffectual; but we assure your Majesty, that however difficult the Talk may be 10 reform, or even restrain, the Desperate and Abandoned, we will nevertheless perfrverc in our serious Endeavours to provide, if it be possible, a more adequate Remedy against such Enormities, being fully persuaded, from an uninterrupted Experience of your Majesty’s Goodness, that we shall be assisted by your Majesty *s Concurrence and Support in every Measure that shall be found expedient in this, or any other Respect, for the Welfare and Mappiness of your People.

A Petition of several of the Trustees, whose Names are thereunder subscribed, appointed to put in Execution an Act, passed in the Twenty-first Year of the Reign of his present Majesty King George the Second, for repairing the High Road leading from Pier abridge to 'Kirkmerrmgton, in the County of Durham, and from thence to the Turnpike Road at lndhoe Lane End, in the said County, was presented to the House, and read; setting forth. That, by the said Act, several Tolls and Powers were granted for repairing the said Road, which were to have Continuance for Twenty-one Years from the First Day of June 1748; but no Provision is made in the said Act, nor any Toll granted, for any Lime, Limestones, or Coals for burning such Limestones into Lime; and that the Tolls for Carriages and Cattle laden with Fire Coal are but very small, and not, as the Petitioners apprehend, equal to the Damage done to the said Road thereby, nor adequate to the other Tolls granted by the said Act; and that, at the Time of passing the said Act, the said Road was in a very ruinous Condition, and the Petitioners borrowed several Sums of Money, which, together with the Tolls collected, have been duly applied according to the Directions of the said Act; and that there is now due, on the Credit of the said Act, the Sum of One thousand Three hundred Pounds, at Five Pounds per Centum per Annum; which hath not been sufficient to repair all the said Road, and which cannot be repaid, and all Parts of the said Road be sufficiently amended, and kept in Repair for the future, unless the Term and Powers granted by the said Act be enlarged: And therefore praying, That Leave may be given to bring in a Bill for enlarging the Term and Powers by the said Act granted, for such Time, and in such Manner, as to the House shall seem meet.

Ordered, That the said Petition be referred to the Consideration of a Committee: And that they do examine the Matter thereof; and report the fame, as it shall appear to them, to the House:

And it is referred to Mr. Vane% Mr. Colleton, Mr. Wilkinjon, Lord Barrington, Lord Hobart, Mr. Hunter, Mr. 6alusbury, Mr. Hay, Mr. Boone, Mr. Gray, Mr. Kynafitm, Lord Dupplin, Mr. Lyster, Mr. Tracy, Mr. Gybbon, Mr. Thornhagb, Mr. Compton, Mr. Wation, Mr. Hardingt, Mr. Vol. 26.

Mr. Charlton, according to Order, reported from the Committee of the whole House, to whom it was referred to consider further of the Supply granted to his Majesty, the Resolutions which the Committee had directed him to report to the House j which he read in his place, and afterwards delivered in at the Clerk’s Table: Where the same were read, and are as followeth j viz.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That a Number of Land Forces, including Eighteen hundred and Fifteen Invalids, amounting to Eighteen thousand Eight hundred and Fifty-seven effective Men, Commission and Non-commission Officers included, be employed for the Service of the Year 1754.

Resolved, That it is the opinion of this Committee, That a Sum not exceeding Six hundred Twenty-eight thousand Three hundred and Fifteen Pounds Seven Shillings and Eleven Pence be granted to his Majesty, for defraying the Charge of the Eighteen thousand Eight hundred and Fifty-seven effective Men for Guards, Garrisons, and other his Majesty’s Land Forces, in Great Britain, Guernsey, and Jersey, for the Year 1754.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That a Sum not exceeding Two hundred Thirty-six thousand Four hundred and Twenty Pounds Eighteen Shillings and Six Pence Half-peny be granted to his Majesty, for maintaining his Majesty’s Forces and Garrisons in the Plantations, Minorca, and Gibraltar and for Provisions for the Garrisons in Nova Scotia, Newfoundland, Gibraltar, and Providence; for the Year 1754.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That a Sum not exceeding One hundred and Eighteen thousand Three hundred and Forty-seven Pounds Twelve Shillings and Four Pence be granted to his Majesty, for the Charge of the Office of Ordnance for Land Service, for the Year j 754.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That a Sum not exceeding Five Thousand Two hundred and Eighteen Pounds Four Shillings and Eight Pence be granted to his Majesty, for defraying the extraordinary Expence of the Office of Ordnance for Land Service, not provided for by Parliament.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That, towards raising the Supply granted to his Majesty, the Sum of Two Shillings in the Pound, and no more, be raised within the Space of One Year, from the 25th Day of March 1754, upon Lands, Tenements, Hereditaments, Pensions, Offices, and personal Estates, in that Part of Great Britain called England, Wales, and Town of Berwick upon \Tweed; and that a proportionable Cess, according to the Ninth Article of the Treaty of Union, be laid upon that Part of Great Britain called Scotland.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That, towards raising the Supply granted to his Majesty, the Duties on Malt, Mum, Cyder, and Perry, which, by an Act of Parliament of the 26th Year of his Majesty’s Reign, have Continuance to the 14th Day of June 1754, be further continued, and charged upon all Malt which shall be made, and all Mum which shall be made or imported, and all Cyder and Perry which shall be made for Sale, within the Kingdom of Great Britain, from the 23d Day of June 1754, to the 24th Day of June 1755.

The said Resolutions, being severally read a Second time, were, upon the Question severally put’ thereupon, agreed to by the House.

Mr. Ker reported from the Committee, to whom the Petition of the Provost, Magistrates, and Council, of the City of Edinburgh, in behalf of themselves, and the other Inhabitants, Merchants and Traders in the said City, the Town of Leith, and other adjacent Places, was referred; That the Committee had examined the Matter of the said Petition; and had directed him to report the fame, as it appeared to them, to the House; and he read the Report in his Place, and afterwards delivered it in at the Clerk’s Table: Where the same was read, and is as followeth; viz.

In Support of the Allegations o,f the said Petition,

Mr. Francis Grant said. That the Harbour of Leith lies at the Mouth of a small River: That about 500 Yards from the lowest Moorings there is a Stone Bridge, beyond which no Ships can pals; and that there are not sufficient Conveniencies below Bridge for building, repairing, wintering, loading, or unloading, of Vessels, so that Ships belonging to Leith and Edinburgh have been obliged to go to Bruntifiand to winter:

That the Witness had made Proposals to Carpenters to build Ships; and had been answered. That there was not sufficient Room in the Harbour for that Purpose; but, upon being alked the Question, he said, That if Ships could pass above the Bridge there would be sufficient Room.

Mr. Tod produced and explained to your Committee a Plan of the said Harbour, and of the intended Improvements; whereby it appeared, that by taking down the present Stone Bridge, and erecting a Draw Bridge in lieu thereof, the said Harbour would be much enlarged; and by purchasing certain Grounds on the Banks of the said River, above the present Bridge, Conveniencies might be made for building, repairing, and loading, of Vessels.

And the Witness said. That Application had been made by the most considerable Traders of Edinburgh and Leith to carry the said Plan into Execution; and that the same had been communicated to the Gentlemen of the adjacent Country, and had met with a general Approbation; and that he believed several Persons would be willing to contribute for that Purpose; and that, if the said Plan should be carried into Execution, it would be of great Advantage to the Inhabitants of Edinburgh and Leith, as well as to the Publick:

That large Sums had been expended in making the said Harbour safe and commodious, by the Magistrates and Council of Edinburgh, without effectually answering those Purposes; notwithstanding which they are willing to advance the further Sum of 2,000l. for carrying the present Plan into Execution; but are unable to do it, without an Act of Parliament, on Account of certain Interests in the Grounds intended for that Purpose.

Mr. William Smith and Mr. John Hay, Masters of Ships, being severally examined, confirmed the above Evidence in every Particular.

Ordered, That Leave be given to bring in a Bill for improving and enlarging the Harbour of Leith; and to im power the Trustees therein to be mentioned to purchase Lands for that Purpose; and for erecting Docks and other Conveniencies on the Sides thereof: And that Mr. Ker and Colonel Haldane do prepare, and bring in, the fame.

The House being informed. That Mr. Lebeup, from the Treasury, attended at the Door:

He was called in; and, at the Bar, presented to the House, pursuant to their Order,

And then he withdrew.

Mr. Chancellor of the Exchequer, by his Majesty's Command, acquainted the House, That his Majesty, having been informed of the Contents of the said Petition, recommends it to the Consideration of the House.

Then the said Petition was brought up, and read; setting forth, That the Petitioners served in his Majesty’s Navy during the late War, and when their Ships were paid off were most of them left destitute of any Support; and that they are the only Officers in his Majesty’s Service who are entirely unprovided for when discharged; and that, when employed, they are of no more Expence to the State than an Ordinary Seaman, the rest of their Pay arising from Deductions out of the Men’s Pay, and is by that means more uncertain than that of any other Officers; and that, by Petition presented to his Majesty soon after the Conclusion of the Peace, they humbly represented their distressed Circumstances, and implored to be Partakers of the same Advantages that their Brethren, the Chaplains of the Army and Marines, and other discharged Officers, were; and that his Majesty was graciously pleased to refer the said Petition to the Commissioners of

Ncftc, &c. sir John Turner reported from the Committee, to whom lvers’ the Petition of the Merchants, Navigators, and other Traders, at the Borough and Port of King’s Lynn, in the County of Norfolk 5 and also the Petition of the Merchants, Navigators, and other Traders and Proprietors of Lands, of the City of Peterborough, in the County of Northampton; and also the Petition of the several Traders and other Inhabitants of the several Towns of Whittlesea, March, Chatteris, Ramsey, Outwell, and Upwell, and other adjoining Places, in the great Level of the Fens called Bedford level-, and also the Petition of the Governor, Bailiffs, and Commonalty, of the Company of Conservators of the great Level of the Fens called Bedford Level; wefe severally referred; That the Committee had examined the Matter of the said Petitions; and had directed him to report the fame, as it appeared to them, to the House; and he read the Report in his place, and afterwards delivered it in at the Clerk’s Table: Where the same was read, and is as followeth; viz.

To prove the Allegations of the said Petitions,

Mr. Langley Edwards said, That he had, about the Ninth of November last, surveyed the River Nene-, and that the fame, from Salter's load Sluice, through Well Creek, by the Town of Outwell, to Floods Ferry, is, in many Places, not above 24 or 2j Feet broad; and the Navigation is so obstructed with Weeds, Silt, and other Foul-nesses, that it is impossible for Boats or other Vessels to pass the same between the Months of March and October; and that from October to March Vessels of Twelve Tons Burthen cannot carry above Three; and that the old Navigation from Floods Ferry to Wrights Bridge, through Whittlesea Meer, Ramsey Meer$ and Ugg Meer, was always

Decembris. A. 1753;

very dangerous, many Vessels having beeri there loft, and it is at present totally impracticable, arid is Eight Mile9 farther than by Whittlesea Dyke, through which the Navigation has for many Years been carried on from Floods Ferry to Standground Sluice; and that the OldBedfcrdRiver, through the Forty Foot Drain, to Chatteris and Ramsey, and from thence to Floods Ferry, is in very bad Condition, and the many shoal Places and Shallows therein render it very difficult for Vessels to get over the fame: And th&

Witness said, he has seen many Stacks of Corn un-threshed, which the Owners informed him they could not remove on Account of the Badness of the River; and that it would be of great Benefit to the Country in general, it the said River was made more navigable.

Matthev.; Wildmore Esquire confirmed the above Evidence; and added, That the Country suffers very much for want of the said River being in good Condition.

The Lord Carysfort reported from the Committee of Distemper the whole House, to whom it was referred to take into "f10*# Consideration the Laws made, and the Rules, Orders, CaiUt* and Regulations, made by his Majesty, more effectually to prevent the Spreading of the Distemper which now rages among the horned Cattle in this Kingdom, the Resolutions which the Committee had directed him to report to the House; which he read in his Place, and afterwards delivered in at the Clerk’s Tabic: Where the same were read, and are as followeth; viz.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee,

That the lodging of Cattle driven for Sale in Places where infected Cattle are, or have lately been, may be one Cause of spreading the Distemper now raging among the horned Cattle of this Kingdom.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee,

That the mixing together different Herds of Cattle, not fit for immediate Slaughter, in Fairs, Markets, and other Places for Sale, has been one other Cause of spreading the Distemper now raging among the horned Cattle of this Kingdom.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee,

That the mixing of infected Cattle with found, irt Commons and common Grounds, has been one other Cause of spreading the Distemper now raging among the horned Cattle of this Kingdom.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee,

That great Difficulties and Inconveniencies have arisen, and may hereafter arise, from the want of proper Powers to order the lodging Cattle stopt by virtue of his Majesty’s Order in Council of March 2 2d 1747.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee,

That the Laws, Rules, Orders, and Regulations, for the killing of infected Cattle upon their first being seized, have not in general been pundtually complied with.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee,

That Certificates for Cattle to be driven beyond the Distance of Five Miles, without a Limitation of Time beyond which such Certificates shall cease to be of Force, arc subject to Abuse, and may have been one other Cause of spreading the Distemper now raging among the horned Cattle of this Kingdom.

Resolved, That ic is the Opinion of this Committee,

That all Contracts and Bargains between the Buyers and Sellers of Cattle, conditional upon such Cattle, or any Number of them, surviving a certain Time, tend to the continuing and further spreading the Distemper now raging among tfce horned Cattle of this Kingdom.

Resolved,

170 Decem.

876

Refoked, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That the Laws, Rules, Orders, and Regulations, now in being, for preventing the Spreading of the Distemper which now rages among the horned Cattle in this Kingdom, be reduced into One Act of Parliament, subject to such Alterations and Regulations as his Majesty, by the Advice of his Privy Council, shall, from time to time, think proper to order.

Resolved, That ic is the Opinion of this Committee, That the Notices ordered to be given of the breaking out, and ceaTing, in particular Places, of the Distemper now raging among the horned Cactle in many Parts of this Kingdom, by his Majesty’s Order in Council of the 22d Day of March 1747, be published in the London Gazette.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That no horned Cattle be driven or admitted into arty Paftflre, Close, or Field, where the Distemper has been, for Two Calendar Months after such Distemper has ceased; nor for SixCalendar Months where such Pastures, Closes, or Fields, have not been cleared of all Litter, Dung, Stover, or Hay, remaining in such Pastures, Closes, or Fields, during the Distemper, and where such Pastures, Closes, or Fields, have not been rolled, mowed, or fed bare with Horses, Hogs, Geese, or Sheep.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That no Certificate for Cattle to be driven beyond the Distance of Five Miles, conformable to his Majesty’s Order in Council, be of Force for any longer Term than Ten Days from the Date of such Certificate.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That no Two or more Herds of Cattle, con filling together of above Twenty Beads, intended for immediate Bale, and not fit for immediate Slaughter, be driven into, or admitted at the same time in, the same Pasture, Close, Field, Fair, Market Place, or other Place of Sale whatsoever, unless such Pasture, Close, Field, Fair, Market Place, or other Place of Sale, be so separated and divided as to preserve the Cattle of such different Herds from immediate Contact.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That no horned Cattle be driven to Pasture in Commons or common Grounds, unless such Cattle have been in the Possession of their Owners, and free from the Distemper now raging among the horned Cattle of this Kingdom, Forty Days at the least before such driving.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That proper Powers be granted for the lodging such Cattle as shall be flopped by virtue of his Majesty’sOrder of Council of March 22d 1747:

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That all Contracts and Bargains between the Buyers and Sellers of Cattle, conditional upon such Cattle, or any Number of them, surviving a certain Time, be void; and that further Penalties be inflicted upon all those who shall so offend.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That a Reward, equal to the full Value, shall be paid to the Owner of every First, Second, and Third Beaftof the whole Stock of horned Cattle upon every Farm or Holding of the same Person, that shall be seized with the Distemper now raging amongst the horned Cattle of this Kingdom, and that shall be separated, killed, and buried, conformable to his Majesty’s Order in Council of March 22d 1747, provided such Beast or Beasts shall have been the real Property, and remained in the actual Possession, of such Owner Forty Days at the least immediately preceding such killing.

Litchfield A Petition of Henry Vernon Esquire was presented to Election. the House, and read; setting forth, That on the 24th Day of November 1753 came on the Election of a Citizen to serve in this Parliament for the City of Litchfield, in the room of the Honourable Richard Levejon Gower Esquire, deceased, at which the Petitioner and Sir Thomas Grefley Baronet, were Candidates; and alleging. That William Brookes Gentleman, Sheriff of the said City of Litchfield, and who was the Returning Officer at this Election, being gained into the Interest of the said Sir Thomas Grefley, did proceed in taking the Poll against the Petitioner with the utmost Partiality, rejecting many legal Votes which were duly tendered for the Petitioner, and admitting great Numbers of Votes in favour of the said Sir Thomas Grefley, who had not the least Colour of Right; and that the principal Magistrates, Town-clerk, and Chamberlain, of the said City, having, previous to the Election, got into their or some of their Custody or Power all the Burgage Books and Rentals of the Chief or Burgage Rents of the said City, and the Books of Enrolments of Freemen in many of the Companies of the said City, and all the original Assessments of the several Parishes there, and other Evidences of a publick Nature, did not only refuse to allow the Petitioner, or his Agents, to take Copies or Extracts thereof, though they were frequently applied to for that Purpose; bur the said Bailiffs and Town-clerk, in concert with the said Sheriff, with a View to deprive the Petitioner of all Means of qualifying and supporting his own Votes, and to di(able him from proving Objections to Sir Thomas Grefley'*, did refuse to let the Petitioner, or his Agents, infpcCt the said Books, Assessments, and Evidences, even when they thought proper to produce the same in Court, in Support of the Claims of Voters who appeared in the Interest of the said Sir Thomas Grefley; and that the Chamberlain of the said City, from the like unjust Motives, refused to appear in Court to give his Testimony touching die Rights of the Burgage Tenants, from wjhom he had or ought to have collected the Burgage or Chief Rents due to the said City, though he was frequently called upon in Court, and applied to for that Purpose; and that by these and divers ocher illegal and undue Methods, made use of by the said Sheriff, Magistrates, Town-clerk, and Chamberlain, of the said City, and by the Agents of the said Sir Thomas Grefley, a Majority was obtained for the said Sir Thomas Grefley; who hath been returned accordingly, notwithstanding the Petitioner had a considerable Majority of legal Votes chac were received or tendered for him, and was duly elected for the said City, and ought to have been returned: And therefore praying the Hous; to take the Petitioner’s same into Con side rat ion, and to give the Pe^ ritioner such Relief in the Premiles as the Nature of his same requires, and as to the House shall seem meet.

APPENDIX, rf*j.

May it please your Lordships,

IN Obedience to your Lordships Desire, we have considered the Stare made by One of the Deputy Auditors of the Account of Thomas Marriott, late Agent and Fay-mailer of Two Troops of Rangers, fcfr. with the Lift of Bills and Certificates, (Ac. transmitted to us the 16th of March last by James West Esquire; as also the Report of the 28th May 1748, and the Lords Justices Warrant of the 4th of Augu/l following, referred to by Mr. West \ togerher with your Lordships Commands to give our Opinion whether there is any, and what Foundation for the making any, further Allowance for Extraordinary Fx pence* exceeding the Savings made out of the Eila-blishment, either upon the Claim of the Possessbrs of the said Bills, or any other Article contained in the said Account.

And we do thereupon humbly report to your Lordships, That ih- Articles in the Discharge the above Account for Payments for sundry Services and extraordinary Expences in Georgia to Michaelmas 1743, amounting to 6,061/. 13/. id. should n t be allowed, as a bum of 66,109/ 13J. lod. was voted by Parliament the 2 2d March 174^, pursuant to an Account of extraordinary Services incurred in Georgia for the Preservation and Defence of his Majesty's Dominions on the Continent of America, fron the 2 2d of September 1738 to the 2zd July 1743, when General Oglethorpe failed for England to the respective times those Services were severally made up to, and from thence computed, to Michaelmas 1743; 2nd likewise because his Majesty’s Warrant of the 23d of March 174^ expressly appoints Mr. Marriott to be Agent and Paymaster from the Commencement of their Lfta-blishment, which was from the 30th of September 1743 incluSve.

We beg Leave to make a general Observarion on the Auditor’s State of the Account to your Lordships, That The Monies granted by Parliament, between Michaelmas 1743 and Middjummer 1747, did exceed the Payments in ihofe Years in the Sum of 2,215/. 15 3^. as may more

particularly appear to your Lordships by an Abstract hereunto annexed of the Monty voted and Payments made; and we are further to observe to your Lordships, on the Objection ma le against several of the Articles, by reason the Store-keeper had not sworn to his Account of lflfues: That Mr. Griffith Wiliams hath since sworn to his Account; a Copy of which is hereunto annexed; which appears very full: We have likewise had him before us, who has given a very satisfactory Account; Moreover we cake Leave to make a further Observation to your Lordships on the said State of the Accomptanc’s Account, That we find Three Articles in the Annual Payments between Michaelmas 1744 and Midsummer 1747, amounting to 7,311/. 19s. nd. for the Charge of the Ship Succejs, mounting 29 Pounders, 6 Pounders, Carriage Guns and Swivel Guns; which, from her Burthen and Sifce, is not, w'e apprehend, within the Georgia Establishment, nor does it appear by what Authority a Ship, being neither a Half-galley nor Schooner, was contracted for; but it does appear, that the said Ship Succejs did not fail for Georgia, buc was employed in England, during the Rebellion, till the 13th of May 1746; which, if by Order of the Government, may be asked of Parliament.

We arc now to report to your Lordships on the several Articles of Extraordinaries, which follow the annual Accounts, ending at Midsummer 1747 first of which is for Provisions and Stores delivered to Colonel Heron at that time, which is by him acknowledged, and ought therefore to be allowed in this Account; amounting to 4,062/. 10s. 9d.

The several Payments and contingent Expences made by Order of General Oglethorpe, alleged to be pursuant to his Majesty’s Pleasure, signified by the Duke of Newcastle, for Ranger Recruits raised in England\ and lent to the North to serve in the late Rebellion, amounting to i,886/. 5/. Vot.. 26.

8S7

ought not to be a Part of this Account; but, if what is Bills drawn alleged be admitted by your Lordships, the same may be . asked of Parliament. iCOr

We are likewise humbly of Opinion, that the next Article of 1,276/. 12*. 3ld. for Charges of bringing up Mings, (Ac. ought not to be a Part of this Account; but, if admitted by your Lordships, may be deemed a Service to be asked of Parliament.

The following Article of 1,815/. I2S- &ems not ro have been within the Scope of Mr. Marriott* Agency, as we know of no Design of adding a Second Battalion to Lieutenant General Oglethorpe's lare Regiment, nor does any Warrant or Authority appear for this Article.

The Article cf 371/. 7s. 4d. to Jacob Franks of New Toth, &q. being for a Service before Michaelmas 1743, we apprehend ought not to be allowed in this Account.

The Claim of 175/. 15*. 6\rd. for Provisions and Cloathing to the Orphans fentto Georgia, ought to be dtf-allowed, his Majesty, having granted a Warrant, dated the 23d of May 1746, for 301/. 12J. which, with former Payments made to Mr. Verelft, was in full Ittisfaction of all Demandson accountofmaintaining,providingwith Ne-ccfiaries, and putting out Apprentices, the said Orphans

The Four following Articles of 600l. 163/. jj. 985/. and 355/. we have no Objection to their being allowed.

The Claim the AccomptantMr. Marriott makes of an Allowance of 30s. a Day, as Agent and Paymaster to these provincial Troops for the Time therein mentioned, amounting to 1,236/. we think reisonable, no other Allowance appearing to us to have been made to him as Agent, and 301. a Day being the ufnal Allowance of a Deputy Paymaster; buc then the following Claims of 141/. 11 s. 6d. and another of 150/. for personal Expences, ought not to be allowed the Accomptant.

The Allowance of 5/. per Cent, amounting to t,o&8/» os. yd. claimed by Griffith Williams, Score-keeper,over and above his Salary, for his Pains and Trouble in purchasing and delivering Stores, (Ac. we think is too large an Allowance; but humbly submit the Quantum to yodr Lordships.

The Two Charges of 79/. js. and 200l. for Fees fbt passing the Account arc, wc suppose, usual.

We have carefully examined and enquired into the State of the Bills, find no Fraud nor Suspicion of Fraud, but that the Credit was given by Merchants as u/ual for Bills drawn; we are therefore most humbly of Opinion* that the Bills, amounting to 151497/. 31. t^d. ought to be paid to the Bill holders; and though it be true, as reported to your Lordships by us the 28th of May 1748* that the Expence should by no means exceed the Establishment, we cannot find any Person to blame, except Mr. Marriott\ forasmuch as he disbursed the Sums, ob-ftrved upon in this Report, in Payments which we conceive he ought not to have made, amounting to no left than 18,869/. 5s. id. so that, had the Payments been confined to Services within the Establishment, there would have been no Deficiency; but, on the contrary, a Surplus in the Hands of this Accomptant.

Which is humbly submicted to your Lordships.

W. Pitt,

H. Fox.

A Petition of the Mayor, Aldermen, Burgesses, and prin- Leicester to cipal Inhabitants of the Borough of Warwick, in the County Coventry of Warwick, was presented to the House, and read; taking Roa<ls* Notice of the Application which has been made to the Houlc for a Bill to repair the Road leading from the Borough of Leicester, in the County of Leicester, to the City of Coventry, and representing to the House, That the Road leading from the City of Coventry to the said Borough of Warwick, and from thence to Halford Bridge, is the usual and ancient Road from the East Parts of this Kingdom, through the Borough of Leicester, and the City of Coventry, to Bristol,

Bath, and other Places in the West; and that the said Road between the said City of Coventry and Halford Bridge aforesaid is, in many Parts thereof, greatly out of Repair, and in general in so bad a State, that it is not likely ever to be repaired by the ordinary Methods of Law:

And therefore praying, That in the said Bill some Provision may be made for the better repairing of the said Road from the City of Coventry, through the Borough of Warwick, to Halford Bridge, in the said County; or that Leave may be given, in favour of the Petitioners, to bring in a proper Bill for repairing the said Road from the City of Coventry to Halford Bridge; or that the Petitioners may have such Relief as the Nature of their same may admit of and require.

Ordered, That the said Petition be referred to the Consideration of the Committee, to whom the Petition of the Gentlemen, Clergy, and Mayor and Aldermen, and other Inhabitants of the City of Coventry, in the County of the said City, and of the Mayor, Aldermen, and other Inhabitants, of the Borough of Leicester, in the County of LeiccJ-ter, and of the Trustees for putting in Execution an Act, passed in the Twenty-fixeh Year of the Reign of his present Majesty, for repairing the Road from the Borough of Leicester, in the County of Leicester, to the Town of Ashby de la Zouch, in the said County, whose Names are thereunto subscribed, is referred: And that they do examine the Matter of this Petition; and report the fame, as it shall appear to them, to the House.

Sail Cloth, at the Ports of Greenock zhdPort GlasgoWy was presented to the House, and' read; setting forth. That by Two Acts of Parliament, of the 12th of Queen Anne, and the 4th of his present Majesty, a Bounty Of Two Pence per Ell was granted on all British-made Sail Cloth exported as Merchandize, to be paid out of the additional Duty of foreign Sail Cloth imported; and that, this Funci having proved inefficient, it was enacted by the 23d 01 his present Majesty, That, for all British-made Sail Cloth exported after the ift of June 1750, the said Bounty should be paid out of that Part of the Old Subsidy that was applicable to Incidents, thereby leaving the Bounty of what was exported before that Period to be paid as formerly out of the Duty of foreign Sail Cloth imported; and that the Petitioners had exported sundry Parcels of Sail Cloth of their own Manufacture before the said First of June 1750, the Bounty on which could not be recovered for want of a FTind on the Branch of foreign Sail Cloth imported; and that there ft ill remains unpaid to the Petitioners, on this Account, the Sum of 1,358/. 11s. rod, as will appear by the several Debentures, regularly certified, and ready to be produced ;and that since the Commencement of the last-mencioned Ad, as well as before, the Petitioners have, at sundry Timet, applied to the respective Collectors for Payment of the said Debentures, without Success, having always had for Answer, That there was no Money in their Hands arising from the Duty of foreign Sail Cloth, and which the said Collectors have accordingly certified on the Foot of the several Debentures; and that the Importation of foreign Sail Cloth having thus entirely failed in North Britain, and there being no Appearance chit any-Fund will again arise from thence, the Petitioners are left without Remedy, by any Law now in being, for the1 Recovery of the Bounty due upon the said Debentures; and alleging. That the Petitioners have fully complied with the Intention of Parliament in granting the said Bounty* and, on the Faith of its being paid, have difeouhted the Value thereof to the several Persons they fold their Sail Cloth to: And therefore prayjpg, r That the said Debentures, being for Sail Cloth exported1 before thei First of June 1750, be paid out of the Old Subsidy; in like Manner as those that were certified after chat: Time'; or, that the House will grant such other Relief in the Premises as to the House shall seem meet.

The said Estimate is as followeth; viz.

I N pursuance of an Address from this House to his Majesty lad Sessions of Parliament, that he would be graciously picafed to give Directions, That an Estimate might be laid before this House, this Sessions, of the Charge of rebuilding the Prison of the Marshafea of the Court of King’s Bench;

The Board of Works have been directed by the Right Honourable the Lords Commissioners of his Majesty’s Treasury, to survey the said Prison; and find it a very ruinous old Building, unsafe for the Custody of Prisoners, and very prejudicial to their Health, so that we think no Money ought to be laid out upon it in Repairs.

On finding it so bad, we desired to know of the Marshal what Number of Prisoners it was necessary to provide for (if a new Building should be erected on the present Ground); who told us, he thought, not less than Two hundred; and that likewise there must be a Chapel, an Apartment for the Marftul, and another for the Master of the Prison, with proper Con veniencies.

APPENDIX, N° 1.

THE following Plan for obtaining an Act of Parlia-. ment for the better draining The North Level, Part of the Great Level of the Fens called Bedford Level, in the Isle of E'y, and Counties of Cambridge, Huntingdon, Northampton, and Lincoln, as bounded an 1 defer! bed in the Act of Charles the Second; and also Porfand, in South Holland, in the said County of Lincoln,

" and such other Lands as the Proprietors shall be desirous to drain, under the Powers of such Act, is offered to the Conhderation of the several Parties intended, by the Direction and Recommendation of his Grace the Duke of Bedford, the Right Honourable the Earl of Lincoln, and Thomas Or by Hunter Esquire.

In order to make the Corporation Lands, within The North Level, a proper Security for the additional Taxes 1 intended to be charged upon those Lands, by the Act now prOposed to be obtained:

It seems necessary, That his Grace the Duke of Bedford and the Earl of Lincoln should give up their respective Claims to the Debt now due to them, amounting to about 19,000/ Five Sixth-parts of which is owing to the Duke of Bedford, and One Sixth-part to the Earl of Lincoln:

It seems Bkewife necessary, That the Proportion chargeable upon The North Level of the Corporation Debts, due at Lady-day 1728, since which Time The North Level has been drained separately from the other Levels, should be ascertained and paid off; and, in order to raise the Money necessary for thatPi]rpose,irisproposed, ThattheProprietors of Lands in The North Level be enabled to buy off the Corporation Taxes, now charged by the Act of the 15th of Charles the Second' upon so much of their Lands as will raile their Proportion of the said Corporation Debts, after the Rate of Thirty Years Purchase, computing the Taxes so to be bought off at a T ax and Quarter; each Proprietor to be at Liberty to subscribe, by a certain Day to be fixed,

APPENDIX, N° 2.

A State of the Revenues and Debt of the Corporation of* Bedford Levels, as the same stood at Lady-day 1752s with the Advantages which will accrue to the Creditors of the Corporation, and the Proprietors of the South and Middle Levels, by permitting the Proprietors of the North Level to be discharged of the Debt, in order to their making a Security for a sufficient Sum of Money, to be raised for their better draining on the Terms which have lately been pro-poled.

It appears, by the Books of the Corporation, That, at Lady-day 1666, the Corporation were Debtors to William then Earl, and afterwards Duke, of Bedford, for Money by him advanced to the Corporation, in the Sum of 32,116/. 13 s. 51 d. for which the Corporation executed a Bond to the Earl.

It also appears, by the said Books, That the Earl accepted the said Sum by Instalments at several Times, without Interest; and that the Whole thereof was not paid him till the 27 th of December 1707.

And a Calculation having been made of the Interest of the said Sum of 12,116/ 13J. $\d. to the several Times of Paymefit thereof, according to the Rate of Interest Money then bore, the same amounts to 19,705/.

7 s. 3 d. which the Earl forgave or remitted to the Corporation; it appearing, that the said principal Sum, and Interest to the several Times of Payment thereof, amounted to the said Sum of 19,705/. 7 s. 3 d. above all the Money paid to the Earl and his Executors on account thereof.

It also appears, by the Corporation Books, That the Duke afterwards advanced several other Sums to the Corporation, to be repaid out of the Rent payable by Sir Charles Orby; all which he also accepted without Interest; and, a Calculation of the Interest thereof having been made, it appears, that the Duke forgave or remitted co the Cor- . poration the further Sum of 446/. 6 j. on that account, making together, with the said Sum of 19,705/. 7 s. 3</. in the Whole 20,151 /. 13 s. 3 d. forgiven or remitted to the Corporation by the Duke; which would otherwise still have remained a Debt upon the Corporation 5 and the Whole of the Duke's Estate being in the North Level,. it may be looked upon as so much of the Corporation Debt discharged by the Proprietors of the North Level.

Reciting, Thac the Duke of Devon, as Guardian to the Duke of Bedford, and Lord Lincoln, had the then last Summer laid out 3,400l. in several Works therein mentioned; which had tended greatly towards the Draining and Prefer vation of all the f states in the said North Level.

But that, by reason of the frequent Floods, and the Insufficiency of the Banks therein mentioned, the said Level had lately been, and was, subject to be drowned, and could not be effectually drained without such new Works as therein are mentioned; and that therefore the said Corporation had resolved to do such new Works, the Charge of which would amount at lead to 6,600l.

That the Duke of Devon, on behalf of the Duke of Bedford, and Lord Lincoln, had agreed, at the kcquest of the Corporation, to advance the said 6,60c/. for the Purposes aforesaid,inproportion to their respective Eftaces in the said Level.

And that the Corporation had agreed, That the Taxes, Revenues, and Rents, of the said North Leiv/only, should be made a Security for Repayment, as well of the said r 3,400l. already laid out, as aforesaid, as of the said

6,600l. to be laid out, with Interest, at 4/. per Cent.; and that the said Corporation were desirous, and had proposed, That the said Duke of Devon, during the Minority of the Duke or Bedford, and afterwards the Duke of Bedford, and the Earl of Lincoln, should not only have . the Direction and Disposal of the said 6,600l. in making the said new Works; but also the Direction, Management, and Difofal of the Taxes, Revenues, and Remsx of the said North Level\ to be employed in repairing and maintaining the Works of the said Level, and making such other Works as should be necessary, and for and towards Payment of the said principal Sums of 3,400l. and 6,600l. and fnterest till the same should be paid.

It is witnessed, That, in consideration of the Premises, and for the Purposes aforesaid, the Corporation did covenant with the Duke of Devon and Earl of Lincoln, Thac the said Duke and Earl, their Agents or Servants, during the Minority of the Duke of Bedford, and after he should have attained his Age, and confirmed this Agreement, for the said Duke of Bedford and Earl of Lincoln, their respective Heirs and Assigns, to take and receive from the Receiver General of the Corporation, the Taxes, Rents, and Revenues, of the said North Level; and that 100l. per Annum, payable by the Heirs and Afligqs of Sir Charles Orby, should be esteemed as Part of the said Revenue.

Provided that the Receiver General should retain so much Money out of the said Taxes and Revenues, as should be sufficient to satisfy the Interest of 2,000l. borrowed by the said Corporation for the Service of the said Level:

That the said Taxes, Revenues, and Rents, should be applied by the said Dukes of Devon and Bedford, and Earl of Lincoln, to the Uses following; viz.

1. For repairing and maintaining all the Works of the said Level, and making and supporting such other Works as should be necessary for draining.

2. For satisfying the Interest, at 4/. per Cent, for the said 3,400l. and 6,6oo/. to the Duke of Bedford and Earl of Lincoln, respectively, according to their respective Proportions.

3. That they should retain and keep the Surplus towards Payment of the said principal Sums, in such Proportions, and by such Payments, as should be reasonable and convenient, untii the same should be fully paid off and satisfied.

Provided, That a just Account should be rendered to the Corporation at their General Aitdit yearly, not only of the Laying out of the said 6,600l. so agreed to be advanced for making the said Works; but also of the Application of the said Taxes, Revenues, and Rents, until the said principal Sums of 3,400l. and 6,60c/. and Interest should be fully p iid and satisfied; and after Satisfaction of the said principal Sums, and Interest, then the said Inden ure. and all the Covenants and Agreements therein, should cease and be void.

Provided, That if the said North Level, or any of the Works thereof, should become chargeable to the Corporation, that then the Taxes, Rents, and Revenues, aforesaid, should, from the Time of its so becoming chargeable, return and belong to the Corporation.

In pursuance of this Agreement, the Duke of Devon,' as Guardian to the Duke of Bedford, and Lord Lincolnt laid out not only the said 6,600l. but also the further Sum of 1,786/. gs. 5Id. (which they submitted to the Loft of, and never brought into any Account) in the Works mentioned in the said Agreement, and passed their Accounts thereof with the Corporation; and the Dukes of Bedford and Lord Lincoln have ever since continued in Receipt of the Taxes and Revenues of the said North Level, and have every Year duly passed their Accounts thereof with the said Corporation; but being obliged by the said Agreement to apply the said Taxes and Revenues, in the First place, in Support of the Works of the said Level, and making such other Works as’should be necessary, and being liable to a Forfeiture of the Benefit of the said Agreement, if the said Level became chargeable to the Corporation, instead of receiving any Parc of their said Debt, a small Part of the Interest thereof has only been paid, so that, at Lady-day 1752, there remained due to the Duke of Bedford and Lord Lincoln, on the Balance of their said Account, the Sum of 18,877/. 3 8d.

which, by the said Agreement, remains an absoluteCharge on the Revenues of the North Level.

And upon these Terms also the Duke of Bedford and Lord Lincoln propose ro surrender the Taxes and Revenues of the North Level to th£ Corpo ation, and it is proposed and intended, that the North Level. and the Taxes and Revenues thereof, shall return to, and continue under the Management and Government of, the Corporation, with this Rcstriction only, That the same be applied to the Service of the North Level only, and not to the Service of the other Levels; and that the North Level be not subject or liable to any future Debts of the Corporation; which is abfedutely necessary, as the Proprietors of the North Level intend to raise further Sums on themselves for draining their Level which would avail them very little, if the Corporation were left at liberty to apply the present Revenues of the Level to other Purposes.

But, in return, it is proposed. That no Part of the Revenues of the other Levels shall be applied to the Service of the North Level; and that the other Levels shall not be subject or liable to any Debts which shall be com-trafted for the Service of the North Level.

The Advantages which will accrue to the Corporation, and the Proprietors of the Middle and South Levels, by carrying these Proposals into Execution, are very manR fest; viz.

First, the Corporation and the other Levels will hereby be entirely freed from the Burthen of the North Level5 which, plainly appears, cannot be supported and preservd by its own Revenues.

Secondly, by yielding up One Eighth of the Revenues of the Corporation, they will be discharged of One Eighth of the Debt, the Intered of which has, ever since 1728, been paid out of the Revenues of the Middle and South Levels, and must not only always so continue to be paid, but the Debt icfelf must also finally tail on those Two Levels only, unless the Debt charged on the North Level, by the Agreement of 1728, should be paid off; which is not likely ever to be; so that this is a clear Gain to the Proprietors of the other Levels.

Thirdly, the Corppration will be discharged of the said Debt of 18,877 /. 3 s. 8d. contracted under the said Agreement of 1728; which, if the Security by that Agreement should prove defective, will fall upon the Taxes and Revenues of the Corporation in general; and which, together with One Eighth of the other Debts, proposed to be discharged by the North Level, amounts to near One Half of the whole Debt of the Corporation, offered to be discharged by the Proprietors of the North Level, in consideration of having their Revenues, but One Eighth of the whole Revenues of the Corporation, discharged of the Residue of the Debt; a Propofalfovcry advantageous to the Proprietors of the other Levels, that it is not apprehended that any Objection can or will be made against ir.

The Counsel were called in.

And one of the Counsel for the Petitioner having proposed to disqualify Seventeen Freemen of the said City, who voted at the said Election for Sir Thomas Grefley y the late fitting Member, as receiving Alms; and also Twenty-six other Freemen of the said City, who voted for the said Sir Thomas Grefley, as having been fraudulently rated; and also Seven other Persons, who voted for the said Sir Thomas Grefley, as receiving Alms; and also Seven other Freemen of the said City, who voted for the said Sir Thomas Grefley, as not having been regularly inrolled; and also Eleven Freeholders of the said City, who voted for the said Sir Thomas Grefley, though they were not rated to the Land Ta* J and also Seven other Freeholders of the said City, who voted for the said Sir Thomas Grefley, as having voted for Parts of Burgage Tenements, for which ocher Persons voted at the said Election; ’

And having also proposed to add to the Poll of the Petitioner Seventeen Freemen of the said City, whole Names, the said Counsel alleged, were left out of the Rates on purpose to disqualify the said Freemen from voting at the said Election;

The said Counsel infilled. That the Votes of the said several Persons whom they proposed to disqualify, being deducted from the Poll of the said Sir Thomas Grefley, and the Votes of the said Seventeen Freemen, last mentioned, being added to the Petitioner’s Poll, the Petitioner had a Majority of legal Votes.

And the said Counsel having offered to produce Evidence, in order to disqualify Persons who had voted for the said Sir Thomas Grefley;

The Counsel on the other Side admitted the several Objections made by the Counsel for the Petitioner to the Votes of the said several Persons, whom the Counsel for the Petitioner had proposed to disqualify; and also admitted the Votes of the said Seventeen Freemen proposed to be added to the Petitioner’s Poll; and acquainted the House, That he was indrafted to give the House no further Trouble.

And then the Counsel on both Sides were directed to withdraw.

A Motion was made, and the Question being put.

That Sir Thomas Grefley Baronet, deceasrd, was duly, eltfted a Citizen to serve in this prefenc Parliament for the Cuv of Litchfield;

It passed in the Negative.

Whitechapel Mr. Cooke reported from the Committee, to whom the poor, &c. Petition of the Churchwardens, Overseers of the Poor, and other Inhabitants of the Parish of Saint Mary Mat* felon, otherwise White Chapel, in the County of Middlesext the Liberty of the Tower of London, and Part of the City of London, was referred; That the Committee had examined the Matter of the said Petition; and had directed him to report the fame, as it appeared to them, to the House; and he read the Report in his Place; and afterwards delivered it in at the Clerk’s Table.

Ordered, That Mr. Cooke have Leave to make a motion, it being after Three of the Clock:

And he moved the House accordingly.

And the said Report was read, and is as followeth; viz. In Support of the Allegations of the said Petition, Alexander Boulton Esquire said. That White Chapel is a very extensive and populous Parish, and maintains be-rween Four and Five hundred poor Persons, at the annual Expence of Two thousand Pounds and upwards; many of whom are able and willing to work if they could have Employment:

That if a Workhouse was erected, under proper Regulations, for the Reception of such poor Persons, there are various Manufactures carried on in the Neighbourhood, in which many of them might be employed; which would greatly reduce the Pbor’s Rates for the future: That the Parish Officers have not proper Powers to oblige the Inhabitants to repair the Highways, and to contribute sufficiently cowards the cleansing, enlightening, and watching, the Streets; which is the Occasion of frequent Robberies and Outrages being committed:

That if the Vestry were enabled to make Rates for the Purposes aforesaid; and if such Rates, together with the Rates for the Relief of the Poor, were put under One Collection, it would be a considerable Saving to the Parish.

Mr. Joseph Gwyne, Constable, said, That no more than Fourteen Watchmen are employed in the-whoje Parish at present.

Mr. Hboyts and Mr. Cope confirmed Mr. Boulton's Evidence, as to the Utility of such a Regulation, and as to the Advantage that would accrue therefrom to the Parish; and added, That such -Regulation was the general Desire of the Inhabitants.

Part of an Act, made in the 25th Year of the Reign of his present Majesty, for repairing and widening the Road leading from Market Harborough, in the County of Lei-cesser, through Dejborough, Rowell, Kittering, Barton Seagrave, and Thrapston, in the County of Northampton, and through Bythorne, Spaldwick, and Ellington, to the Pound in the Parish of Brampton, in the County of Huntingdon, was read; whereby several Powers were given to the Commissioners therein named to erect Turnpikes and Side-gates on any Part of the said Road, and to divert and turn the said Road as they should think most convenient.

Mark Day, Surveyor to the Trustees for the Division between Market Harborough and Thrapston, said. That the said T ruftccs, by virtue of the said Act, have turned the Road which leads from Market Harborough aforesaid, ovtvChain Bridge, through the Turnpike upon the Northampton Road, into Little Bowden, in the County of Northampton, over Clack Hill, towards Dejborough aforesaid, and have carried the same from Market Harborough aforesaid, through a Lane there called St. Mary s Lane, in Market Harborough aforesaid, along Part of the Road there leading towards Saint Mary's Bridge, near Market Harborough aforesaid, over the Welland River, through a Lane called The Church Lane, into Little Bowden aforesaid, where it comes into the said old Road, leading over Clack Hill towards Dejborough aforesaid.

And he produced a Book of the Trustees 5 and an Order therein was read for erecting a Turnpike between St. Mary's Lane and St, Mary's Bridge; and said. That the said Turnpike was erected accordingly.

Benjamin Chapman produced a Warrant, signed by the Commissioners, for taking Toll at the said Turnpike; and said, That Toll had been taken in pursuance of chat Order for about Fourteen Months.

John Smith, Keeper of the Market Harborough Turnpike Gate, in the Road leading to Northampton, was examined; and said, That if the said Turnpike between St. Mary's Lane and Si. Mary's Bridge was removed, it would very much prejudice the Market Harborough Turnpike.

And, being asked if he had made any Computation what the Loss would be, he said he had; and believed it would be between 40 /. and 50 /. per Annum; and said. That, before the Turnpike on the new Road was erected, Horsesand Cattle used to avoid the Gate by going through Little Bowden; and that thereupon he complained to the Commissioners, who ordered a Gate to be erected at that Place.

Mr John Dexter, Clerk to the Trustees for the Division between Market Harborough and Thrapston, being examined, said, That 4,000l. had been borrowed on the Credit of the T oils arising on that Part of the Road lying between Market Harborough and Thrapston; and that, if the said Turnpike between St. Mary's Lane and St. Mary's Bridge was taken down, it would leflfen the Tolls so much, that they should not be able to borrow Money sufficient to finish the Road, nor to pay the Money already borrowed, and Interest for the fame.

And, being asked whether, if the Gate was put in any other Place, they could have borrowed so much Money, said, he apprehended they could not; because the Country is so open, and there are so many Outlets, that they could not have fixed the Turnpike any-where so commodious to prevent Persons avoiding the Payment of the Toll.

Mr. "Thomas Thong, Clerk to the Trustees for the Division between Thrapston and Brampton Pound, being examined, said, That he was present at the First Meeting of the Commissioners, as Clerk; when an Order was made for erecting a Turnpike between «9/. Mary's Lane and S/. Mary's Bridge near Harborough.

A. 1754.

And, being asked whether any Objections were made it that Meeting to the erecting the said Turnpike, he said there was none; and that all the Commissioners present were unanimous in that Order; and that there was an Order made also at that Meeting for borrowing 7,000l. on the Credit of the whole Toll; 4,000 /. for One Division, and 3,000l. for the other \ which was boriowed accordingly.

Mr. Robert Nurjey, being examined, said. That he knows both the old and new Road, and thinks the new Road to be the moll convenient.

And, being asked whether the new Road interfered with the Northampton Turnpike, said it did not; but if ic had gone the old Way it would; and further said. That no Gate could be erected any-where so commodious as the present.

The Lord Strange reported from the Committee, to whom the Petition of the several Persons, whose Names are thereunto subscribed, inhabiting within the Town of Manchester, in the County Palatine of Lancaster; and also the Petition of several Hatters, Dyers, Brew’ers, Whitfters, Calenderers, and other Manufacturers and Traders, within or near the Towns of Manchester and Salford, in the County Palatine of Lancaster, whose Names are thereunto subscribed, in' behalf of themselves, and all other the Manufacturers and Traders within the said Towns and Parts adjacent; were referred; That the Committee had examined the Matter of the said Petitions; and had directed him to report the fame, as it appeared to them, to the House; and he read the Report in his Place, and afterwards delivered it in at the Clerk’s Table: Where the same was read: and is as followeth; viz.

In Support of the Allegations of the said Petitions,

Mr. Samuel Horridge said. That the Inhabitants of the Towns of Manchester, Saford, and Places adjacent, con-fume great Quantities of Coals and other Fuel, all which are brought by Land Carriage; and that no Coals are used in Manchester, but what must be brought Four Miles, and some 10 Miles; the Carriage whereof is a greater Expence than the prime Cost of the Coals.

Mr. 'Taylor said, That he had taken a Level and that a Channel may be made from Salford to within Half a Mile of Wigan, and supplied with W ater from the River Irwell, sufficicnc for the Floating of Vessels, without the lead Prejudice to the Navigation of the said River, as the Water will run into the River again before the Navigation begins:

Thar, by means of this Channel, the Carriage of Coals and Manufactures of all Sorts will be greatly facilitated to and from the said Towns and Places adjacent, and also tendered less expensive by one half than at present.

Robert Gibson said, That he assisted in taking the Level for the said Channel; and, being asked if he thought it practicable to make the Channel in the Manner proposed, he said he did, as the Fall from the River is so great that the Channel may be filled, and constantly supplied with Water, without any Difficulty.

Mr. Ege ton, Guardian to the Duke of Bridgewater, informed your Committee, That he consents to the making a Channel, as proposed, as he thinks it will be of Advantage to his Grace, through whose Lands it is intended to be carried.

And Mr. Taylor said, That the Proprietors of the greatest Part of the Lands, through which such Channel is proposed to be carried, have already given their Contents thereunto.

Ordered, That Leave be given to bring in a Bill for making a navigable Channel from a certain Place in the Township of Salford, to the Town of Leigh, and from thence to or near the Town of Wigan, in the County Palatine of Lancaster, and performing all other WTorks relating the reto: And that the Lord Strange and Mr. Warburton do prepare, and bring in, the fame.
